excerpt: Playco is a Tokyo-based instant-play games company founded by Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron and Michael Carter. It debuted in 2020 with a $100 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation.
content:
Playco describes itself as the world's first instant-play gaming company. Its idea is that a game should start the moment someone taps a link, inside the apps people already use, with no download or install, and that friends should be able to play together straight away. According to its launch press release, Playco built a browser-based streaming game engine meant to run across messaging apps, cloud streaming, Google Play Instant and iOS App Clips, and planned free-to-play games paid for by in-game purchases and opt-in advertising. Its about page names Facebook, LINE, Zoom, Microsoft and Discord among the platforms it works with.

The founders bring long gaming and web histories. Michael Carter, co-founder and CEO, previously co-founded Game Closure, the studio behind the Facebook instant game EverWing, and Playco's site credits him with work on the HTML5 WebSocket standard. Justin Waldron, co-founder and president, co-founded Zynga in 2007. Takeshi Otsuka, a co-founder and executive producer, led Japan's Mobage platform, and Teddy Cross is co-founder and chief product officer.

Playco launched publicly on 21 September 2020 with a $100 million Series A at a valuation of just over $1 billion, making it a unicorn before releasing a game. The round was led by Josh Buckley and Sequoia Capital Global Equities, and TheWrap reported other backers including Will Smith's Dreamers VC, Sozo Ventures, Caffeinated Capital, the Makers Fund, Digital Garage and Taizo Son's Mistletoe. The company announced launch partnerships with Facebook, LINE Messenger, Rakuten Viber and Snapchat, and said it was based in Tokyo, incorporated in Delaware and distributed-first.

Playco's games are free to play; it does not sell subscriptions, and its site lists no current titles or prices.

This page is research, not a review. We have not played Playco games; facts come from the company's pages and the reporting under Sources.
